findings.text: The routine scx_cid_init builds compact identifier tables for a scheduler instance of type scx_sched from online topology then packs remaining possible processors. Caller supplies scheduler context and receives numeric status with negative values signalling allocation or consistency failures. Construction covers bidirectional translation, shard placement, per-identifier topology records and shard range summaries.

Mask helpers of type scx_cmask mutate caller storage over a declared identifier interval. Clearing helper scx_cmask_clear empties the interval while filling helper scx_cmask_fill sets it. Combination helpers provide conjunction through scx_cmask_and, disjunction through scx_cmask_or, selective replacement through scx_cmask_copy and conjunction with negation through scx_cmask_andnot. Only overlapping portions affect the destination.

Predicate helpers query masks without mutation. Helper scx_cmask_subset tests whether every set bit of a mask appears in a different mask, helper scx_cmask_intersects tests whether a bit is set in the shared portion of a pair, and helper scx_cmask_empty tests whether a mask holds no set bits. Out-of-range set bits cause the subset test to report false.

Scheduler exposes extension callables to replace layout during initialization through scx_bpf_cid_override, translate toward processors through scx_bpf_cid_to_cpu, translate toward identifiers through scx_bpf_cpu_to_cid, and retrieve topology detail through scx_bpf_cid_topo. Replacement is restricted to the initialization phase while translation and query serve steady-state use.

Validation and translation helpers centralize range checks. Helper cid_valid accepts only identifiers within the dense range while helper scx_cpu_valid and its inner check __cpu_valid accept only possible processor numbers below the system limit. Translators scx_cid_to_cpu and scx_cpu_to_cid combine validation with table lookup and report scheduler errors plus negative status on failure.

Callable sets scx_kfunc_set_init_cids and scx_kfunc_set_cid register identifier interfaces with module ownership. The initialization set carries an additional context filter restricting its members to the identifier-initialization phase. The general set carries no such filter.

Compact identifiers form a dense sequence covering every possible processor without duplication starting from the initial valid value. Tables cpu_to_cid and cid_to_cpu are mutual inverses so round-trip translation returns the original value. Override input is rejected when any identifier repeats or falls outside the dense range, leaving prior tables unchanged.

Shards partition the identifier sequence into contiguous non-overlapping intervals in increasing order recorded in cid_to_shard. Each shard span respects a configured upper bound capped by an absolute per-shard maximum. Range summaries in shard_ranges record the base identifier and population count for every shard with total count in nr_shards, rebuilt whenever layout changes.

Online processors receive hierarchical placement in topo recording shard, core, cache domain and NUMA node membership with both a representative identifier and a compact ordinal for each level. Processors lacking usable topology receive the marker SCX_CID_TOPO_NEG for all levels except shard membership which remains valid. Query of unknown topology or error cases yields all bits set in the caller buffer.

Mask operations described by base and nr_cids affect only words intersecting the declared interval in bits and preserve outside bits. Partial edge words are masked to the covered subset while fully covered interior words use a full mask. Empty overlap performs no storage access and predicate walks report false without touching memory.

Subset evaluation scans any portion of the candidate interval extending before or after the container interval. Discovery of any set bit in those extensions immediately yields a negative answer because such bits cannot be contained. Only when extensions are clear does evaluation compare the shared interval for missing bits.

Emptiness means no bit is set anywhere inside the declared interval. A helper tests an arbitrary sub-interval for any set bit and returns false for empty or inverted bounds. The any-set operation CMASK_OP1_ANY_SET shares the same edge-masking discipline as mutating walks across different span widths.

Extension program to scheduler resolution returns null for dead schedulers flagged in dead and for missing associations. A variant prefers the program-associated operations structure then falls back to the global root scx_root with compatibility handling for legacy unassociated programs including a warning suppressed after initial occurrence. The simpler variant consults only the global root and its liveness flag.

Mask reference construction snapshots start, count and capacity with ordered reads then rejects starts beyond the possible count, counts extending past the end, and capacities smaller than the words spanned as computed by SCX_CMASK_NR_WORDS. Accepted references record the snapshot and the derived shard span for later bounded walks.

Home node derivation counts member processors per node then selects the index with the strictly greatest count. Ties retain the earliest index and absence of any positive count yields the absent-node marker.

Table construction requires stability of the online processor set and exclusive access to scheduler enablement. The routine asserts both conditions on entry and runs before publication so no concurrent reader can observe partial tables. Allocation uses blocking reclaimable memory.

Layout replacement runs under scheduler enablement exclusion while tables remain unpublished and inside a read-side critical section for scheduler lookup. All blocking allocations and copies of extension-supplied arrays occur before entering the critical section so no blocking operation happens while protected.

Translation and topology query enter a read-side critical section to obtain the scheduler instance and dereference shared tables. They hold no enablement exclusion and perform no mutation. Absence of a live scheduler or of published tables yields an error status rather than dereferencing invalid memory.

Per-identifier topology record of type scx_cid_topo carries eight [CITED] fields. Shard membership uses shard_cid for the representative and shard_idx for the ordinal. Core membership uses core_cid and core_idx in the same pattern. Cache domain uses llc_cid and llc_idx. Node uses node_cid and node_idx. Negative values denote unknown levels.

Mask header of type scx_cmask describes a bit set over a contiguous interval. Field base gives the start offset while field nr_cids gives the population count. Field bits points to word storage indexed relative to the start rounded down to word granularity. Field alloc_words gives capacity which must cover the spanned words.

Table collection of type scx_cid_tables holds forward translation in cid_to_cpu with reverse translation in cpu_to_cid. Per-identifier shard assignment lives in cid_to_shard while per-identifier detail lives in topo. Per-shard home node lives in shard_node with per-shard ranges in shard_ranges and total count in nr_shards. Reverse entries for unassigned processors use a negative sentinel distinct from every valid identifier.

Each shard range record holds base_cid for the shard start and nr_cids for membership. Each shard also stores a home node in shard_node selected as the node owning the most member processors, or an absent-node marker when no member has a valid node. Unused slots beyond the active count are zeroed on rebuild.

Validated mask reference of type scx_cmask_ref snapshots start offset in base plus count in nr_cids for the interval. Scheduler pointer in sch accompanies source header pointer in src. Shard span from shard_first up to but excluding shard_end covers the interval as derived from shared assignment at endpoints. Empty intervals collapse the span to a boundary.

Construction proceeds from allocation and sentinel fill through grouped assignment of online processors by node then cache domain then core with shard splitting, then packing of unassigned possible processors into bounded shards, then warning for degraded topology, then derivation of range summaries and publication of the shard count.

Replacement follows snapshot then validate then install. Snapshot copies extension arrays cpu_to_cid and shard_start under count bounds. Validation checks counts, boundary order and span limits, identifier range and uniqueness. Installation rewrites translations, derives home nodes by majority, resets topology to unknown except shard fields, and rebuilds ranges and count.

Within a cache domain, cores accumulate into the current shard until either a per-shard core budget or a per-shard identifier budget would be exceeded. On overflow a new shard begins at the next identifier with the same home node. Empty shards are never created and shards never cross cache domain boundaries in the default layout.

Table builder serves as the initialization entry invoked while scheduler enablement is held and processor set is stable. It returns success on full construction and negative status on allocation failure or internal topology inconsistency without partial publication.

Override callable scx_bpf_cid_override serves as the initialization-time extension entry for custom layouts. It is registered in a filtered callable set scx_kfunc_set_init_cids restricted to the identifier-initialization context. Invocation outside that context or without a live scheduler has no effect beyond error reporting.

Translation callables scx_bpf_cid_to_cpu and scx_bpf_cpu_to_cid plus topology query scx_bpf_cid_topo serve as steady-state extension entries registered in the general set scx_kfunc_set_cid. Each resolves the calling program to its scheduler, validates its scalar argument, and returns either a translated value or a negative error marker, or fills the caller buffer.

Extension memory may change concurrently so the implementation snapshots counts and arrays before validation and uses ordered accesses for mask words shared with extensions. Validation operates only on snapshots, preventing time-of-check versus time-of-use changes between checks and installation.

Processors without node information are deferred from grouped assignment to the ungrouped tail. Cache domains lacking cache information fall back to node membership for grouping and emit a warning. Online processors that still lack usable topology after grouping emit a separate warning but still receive valid identifiers and shards.

All failure paths during replacement report through the scheduler error channel and return without mutating shared tables. Boundary order, span limits, count mismatches, allocation failures and duplicate assignments each abort before any write. Callers therefore observe either the prior layout or a fully installed new layout.

Predicate walks distinguished by cmask_op2_is_pred stop at a word whose masked result decides the answer, avoiding scans of later words. Non-predicate walks always visit every overlapping word. Empty intervals bypass word access entirely, which also avoids edge cases on empty ranges.

Implementation enforces a compile-time ceiling of 8192 [CITED] possible processors for mask sizing, uses 64 [CITED] bit words for mask storage with head and tail partial-word masking, and reserves -1 [CITED] as the unmapped reverse-translation sentinel distinct from every valid identifier.

Shard sizing honors a scheduler-provided size with a built-in default identified by SCX_CID_SHARD_SIZE_DFL when unspecified, capped by an absolute per-shard maximum identified by SCX_CID_SHARD_MAX_CPUS. Both default construction and override validation enforce the cap so no shard exceeds it even with large configured sizes.

Operations of family cmask_op2 distinguish predicate kinds for subset via CMASK_OP2_SUBSET and intersection via CMASK_OP2_INTERSECTS from mutating kinds for copy via CMASK_OP2_COPY, conjunction via CMASK_OP2_AND, disjunction via CMASK_OP2_OR and conjunction with negation via CMASK_OP2_ANDNOT, plus ordered variants for memory shared with extensions via CMASK_OP2_REF_COPY and CMASK_OP2_REF_OR. Operations of family cmask_op1 provide an any-bit-set test. Only predicate kinds trigger early exit.

Allocation exhaustion reports through ENOMEM while invalid arguments report through EINVAL, each as a negative status. Absent NUMA information uses the marker NUMA_NO_NODE for shard homes and deferred processors. Topology queries represent unknown fields as all bits set.
